newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom's Pacific Star sells customer base - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Telecom's Pacific Star sells customer base - NZPA.

text.p: United States company RSL Communications has bought the commercial customer base of Telecom's loss-making Australian subsidiary Pacific Star for an undisclosed sum, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
Telecom has been offering the assets of Pacific Star for sale since January.

In the run-up to deregulation of the Australian telecommunications market, RSL Com Australia is using the acquisition as its entry point into the Australian market to create a long-distance phone company called Australia Star.

RSL Com is a subsidiary of RSL Communications, a member of the Ronald S Lauder group of companies. It is a relatively new player in the global telecommunications market and was founded by Ronald Lauder, son of cosmetics empress Estee Lauder.
Adrian Coote, the managing director of RSL Com, said Australia Star, based in Brisbane, would continue to manage the 1700 commercial customers held by Pacific Star.

He would not disclose the price paid to Telecom for the customer base, which excludes the Queensland and West Australian government contracts. The contract with the Queensland government expires in August.
"It will focus on providing these customers with the highest levels of service, and will draw on the experience and expertise of the parent company," he said.
The customers are in the small and medium-sized business area, though Coote would not name any of them.
"Our strategy is to focus on communications-intensive small and medium-sized customers," he said.

Australia Star has 18 staff, including 12 who have joined from Pacific Star. It is developing its own billing system which is expected to go live sometime in June or July, "depending on the cleanliness of the cut-over", Coote said.
Australia is RSL's starting point for an Asia-Pacific presence, he said.
It will form a strategic relationship with a local switched service vendor though it expects to put its own switches in.
Coote said RSL Com had not signed any interconnect agreements with carriers in Australia.
